mainTopic: Securing a door on שבת with a bolt or other כלי without it looking like building, and when spreading a covering on שבת counts as making a forbidden אהל.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the earlier מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי about a bolt with a knob whose rope is too weak to lift it. A new משנה follows. The תנא קמא allows a dragging bolt only in the מקדש and forbids a resting bolt everywhere, while רבי יהודה is one level more lenient for each. שמואל rules like רבי יהודה on the dragging bolt, and רבא adds that it must be tied to the door itself, and firmly, not with a reed. A bolt pressed into the ground is forbidden, following רבי יהודה, because it looks like בונה. A bolt with a handle, a huge beam, and a huge mortar all count as a כלי, so they may be used to secure a door. The גמרא then turns to tents on שבת: one may not make a new אהל, but one may add to an existing temporary one, as with boat arches and רב הונא's rolled-up mat. A curtain and a bridal canopy may be put up and taken down on שבת. רב ששת בריה דרב אידי begins listing limits on the canopy based on the width of its top, and the last of these continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי really disagree
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is about a bolt whose rope cannot carry its weight. רבי יוסי says the knob alone makes it a כלי. רבי אליעזר says the knob is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where it cannot be lifted by its rope. One Sage holds: since it has a knob at its end, it has the status of a vessel. The other Sage holds: since it cannot be lifted by its rope, no, it is not a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: in exactly what case do רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי argue about a bolt with a knob? The answer is when the bolt's rope is too thin to lift it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a rope strong enough to lift the bolt shows that the bolt is a real, attached כלי. Here the rope is too weak, so that proof is missing. רבי יוסי says the knob (גלוסטרא) by itself gives it תורת כלי. רבי אליעזר says that without a usable rope, the knob does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be lifted by its rope or binding
A knob or thick end on the bolt
The legal status of a vessel or utensil
"This Sage holds", a formula that introduces each side's reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: For a bolt with a knob, the argument is only about a weak rope. רבי יוסי: the knob makes it a כלי. רבי אליעזר: no usable rope means it is not a כלי.

phrases.english: In a case where it cannot be lifted by its rope,
phrases.notes: The rope is too thin to hold the bolt's weight.

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּיֵשׁ בְּרֹאשׁוֹ גְּלוֹסְטְרָא —
phrases.english: for this Sage holds: since it has a knob at its end,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: it has the status of a vessel.
phrases.notes: So locking the door with it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאֵינוֹ נִיטָּל בְּאִיגְדּוֹ — לֹא.
phrases.english: And this Sage holds: since it cannot be lifted by its rope, no.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר. The knob does not make it a כלי.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיטָּל בְּאִיגְדּוֹ, דְּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer, begun on the previous amud, to the question of where רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי disagree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what exact case do רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי disagree about the knobbed bolt?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the bolt cannot be lifted by its rope. The question is whether the knob alone gives it תורת כלי.

steps.title: משנה: dragging bolt allowed only in the Temple; resting bolt forbidden everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a bolt that drags on the ground may lock a door in the מקדש but not in the מדינה. A bolt that rests on the ground is forbidden in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bolt that drags: one may lock with it in the Temple, but not in the country. And one that rests on the ground is forbidden here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The first opinion ranks two kinds of bolts by how strict we should be about locking a door with them on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dragging bolt is attached but does not hang neatly. Using it is only a rabbinic problem, and rabbinic שבות rules do not apply in the מקדש, so it is allowed there. A resting bolt is not attached at all, so using it looks like building (בונה). That is too serious to allow even in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: A bolt or bar used to lock a door
The one that drags along the ground
We lock (a door)
The Temple / the rest of the country outside the Temple
The one lying or resting on the ground, not attached

phrases.english: MISHNA: A bolt that drags along the ground —
phrases.notes: It is attached to the door, but the rope is long and it drags.

phrases.english: one may lock with it in the Temple,
phrases.notes: אין שבות במקדש: rabbinic decrees do not apply in the Temple.

phrases.english: but not in the country.
And one that rests on the ground is forbidden here and there.
phrases.notes: It is forbidden both in the Temple and outside, because it looks like building.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נֶגֶר הַנִּגְרָר — נוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on the same theme of bolts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dragging bolt: permitted in the מקדש only. Resting bolt: forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: רבי יהודה is one level more lenient
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits the resting bolt in the מקדש and the dragging bolt even in the מדינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the resting one is permitted in the Temple, and the dragging one in the country.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion and moves each kind of bolt one step toward leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a dragging bolt is attached enough to count as a normal כלי, so it is fine everywhere. A resting bolt is only a rabbinic concern, so it is fine in the מקדש. What the תנא קמא calls a real building problem, רבי יהודה treats as only a שבות.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה says, introducing a disagreeing opinion
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: The words "permitted in the country" for the dragging bolt mean it is permitted in the מדינה as well as in the מקדש. They do not mean it is permitted only outside the Temple.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the resting one is permitted in the Temple,
and the dragging one in the country.
phrases.notes: That is, even outside the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַמּוּנָּח מוּתָּר בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Resting bolt: permitted in the מקדש. Dragging bolt: permitted everywhere.

steps.title: ברייתא defines the dragging bolt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains what the תנא קמא means by a dragging bolt: one that is tied and hanging, with one end touching the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which is the dragging bolt that one may lock with in the Temple but not in the country? Any that is tied and hanging, and one end reaches the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to define the term "dragging bolt" from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This bolt is attached and hanging, but because one end touches the ground, it is not treated as fully connected to the door. That is why the תנא קמא allows it only in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Rabbis taught", introducing a ברייתא
Which is it? A request for a definition
Tied and hanging
Reaches the ground

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Which is the dragging bolt
with which one may lock in the Temple but not in the country?
Any that is tied and hanging,
phrases.notes: It is tied to the door.

phrases.english: and one of its ends reaches the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵיזֶהוּ נֶגֶר הַנִּגְרָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term נגר הנגרר from the משנה in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא's dragging bolt is tied and hanging with one end on the ground. It is allowed only in the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי יהודה redefines which bolt is Temple-only
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits the tied, hanging bolt everywhere. For him, the Temple-only bolt is one that is not tied at all and is put away in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: This one is permitted even in the country. Rather, which is the bolt one may lock with in the Temple but not in the country? Any that is neither tied nor hanging, and one removes it and puts it in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה rejects the תנא קמא's example. He gives his own definition of the bolt that is allowed only in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied at all is enough, for רבי יהודה, to permit the bolt everywhere. Only a fully loose bolt, which is removed and stored in a corner, is limited to the מקדש. This matches his opinion in the משנה that the מונח is permitted in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Even in the country outside the Temple
Rather, introducing a corrected version
He removes or pulls it out
A corner

steps.confusionAlert: The same physical bolt is described differently by each opinion. The loose bolt put in a corner is the מונח of the משנה. The תנא קמא forbids it everywhere, while רבי יהודה allows it in the מקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: tied and dragging is allowed in the מקדש only, and loose is forbidden everywhere. רבי יהודה: tied is allowed everywhere, and loose is allowed in the מקדש only.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
this one is permitted even in the country,
phrases.notes: This refers to the tied, hanging bolt.

phrases.english: Rather, which is the bolt
with which one may lock in the Temple but not in the country?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא קָשׁוּר וְלֹא תָּלוּי,
phrases.english: Any that is neither tied nor hanging,
and one removes it and places it in a corner.
phrases.notes: This is the same as the משנה's מונח.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זֶה אַף בַּמְּדִינָה מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the definition in step 4 and lines it up with רבי יהודה's view in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tied bolt is permitted everywhere. A loose bolt that is stored in a corner is permitted only in the מקדש.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה on the dragging bolt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה about a bolt that drags on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי יהודה regarding a dragging bolt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a practical ruling. In the argument from the earlier steps, we follow רבי יהודה about the dragging bolt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a bolt that is tied and hanging, with one end touching the ground, may be used even outside the מקדש. So this ruling permits that kind of bolt everywhere. This is the lenient side of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law that we follow
A bolt that drags on the ground (tied and hanging, with one end touching the ground)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the base for everything that follows. The next steps add conditions to it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda regarding a dragging bolt.
phrases.notes: So the tied, hanging bolt is permitted even outside the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנִגְרָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה laid out in steps 2–5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה: a dragging bolt may be used on שבת even outside the מקדש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We permit the tied, hanging, dragging bolt everywhere.

steps.title: רבא adds that the bolt must be tied to the door
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the ruling: the dragging bolt is only permitted if it is tied to the door itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: And this applies only when the bolt is tied to the door.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to שמואל's ruling. The bolt is only permitted if it is tied to the door itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יהודה is not enough by itself. The bolt must be attached to the door, so it counts as part of the door. Then putting it in place is not like building.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied
Door

phrases.english: Rava said: And that is only when it is tied to the door.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בַּדֶּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling of step 6 by adding a condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dragging bolt is permitted only if it is tied to the door itself.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי טבלא in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: רבי טבלא saw a bolt hanging from the side of the door, not tied to the door itself, and he said nothing against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי טבלא came to מחוזא and saw a bolt hanging from the side of the doorway, and he did not say anything to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's condition. It brings a story where a great rabbi saw a bolt that was not tied to the door, and he did not object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bolt in מחוזא hung from the side of the doorway, not from the door itself. If רבא were right, רבי טבלא should have stopped them. His silence suggests that such a bolt is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (an opening that shows surprise and leads into a challenge)
Happened to come to a place
מחוזא, a town in Babylonia
The side of the doorway

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַבִּי טַבְלָא אִיקְּלַע לְמָחוֹזָא,
phrases.english: Is that so? But Rabbi Tavla happened to come to Mechoza,
and he saw a certain bolt that was hanging
from the side of the doorway,
and he did not say anything at all to them?
phrases.notes: His silence is treated as permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַבִּי טַבְלָא אִיקְּלַע לְמָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's condition from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that the bolt must be tied to the door itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bolt hanging from the side of the doorway was allowed by רבי טבלא's silence, so tying it to the door should not be required.

steps.title: That bolt could be lifted by its rope
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the מחוזא bolt could be picked up by its rope. That makes it a כלי, so it is permitted even without being tied to the door.
steps.simpleTranslation: That bolt was one that could be picked up by its rope.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The bolt in מחוזא was a different kind, so it does not disprove רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bolt whose rope is strong enough to lift it counts as a proper כלי. That kind is permitted everywhere, even if it is not tied to the door. רבא's condition is only about the weaker, dragging bolt.

keyTerms.meaning: Can be picked up by its rope (the rope carries its weight)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of bolts. A bolt that can be lifted by its rope is fine everywhere. Only a dragging bolt, whose rope cannot carry it, needs to be tied to the door itself.

phrases.english: That one was a bolt that could be picked up by its rope.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא נִיטָּל בְּאִיגְדּוֹ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 and protects רבא's condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (a different kind of bolt)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the מחוזא bolt was a dragging bolt that was not tied to the door.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was a bolt that could be lifted by its rope, which is permitted anyway. רבא's condition stands for dragging bolts.

steps.title: רב אויא forbids a bolt tied with a reed
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא saw a man in נהרדעא tying a bolt with a reed. He ruled that the door may not be locked with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא came to נהרדעא and saw a man tying a bolt with a reed. He said: This one may not be used to lock the door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how the bolt must be tied. A weak tie, like a reed, does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the bolt is tied, the tie must be strong and lasting. A reed is too weak, so the bolt is not really attached. Using it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a Babylonian town
A reed (a weak material for tying)
We may lock (with לָא: we may not lock)

phrases.english: Rav Avya happened to come to Nehardea,
he saw a certain man
who was tying the bolt with a reed.
He said: With this one, we may not lock the door.
phrases.notes: The reed is too weak to count as a real tie.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַוְיָא אִיקְּלַע לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical detail to רבא's rule: the tie must be strong.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bolt tied only with a reed is not properly tied, and the door may not be locked with it on שבת.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about a bolt pressed into the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks what the law is if the bolt is pressed into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: If the bolt was pressed into the ground, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a new question about another kind of bolt. This sets up רב יוסף's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing the bolt into a hole in the ground may look like fixing something into the ground, which is like building. So רבי זירא is unsure whether it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (a real question that needs an answer)
Pressed or pushed into the ground
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked: If it was pressed into the ground, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a different type of bolt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a bolt pressed into the ground permitted on שבת, or is using it like building?

steps.title: רב יוסף answers from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף is surprised by the question, because a ברייתא already deals with it. The תנא קמא permits a pressed-in bolt, and רבי יהודה forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Why is he asking? Did he not hear what was taught: If the bolt slipped off its rope, it is forbidden. If it was pressed into the ground, it is permitted. And רבי יהודה says: If it was pressed in, even though it did not slip off, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רבי זירא. A ברייתא already discusses this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bolt fully slipped off its rope, it is no longer attached, so all agree it is forbidden. A pressed-in bolt is the point of argument: the תנא קמא permits it, and רבי יהודה forbids it, even while it is still tied. Here רבי יהודה is the stricter one, unlike in the dragging-bolt case.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is he asking? (the answer is already known)
That was taught in a ברייתא
Slipped off or came loose (from its rope)

steps.whatToRemember: The bolt may be used if it is a כלי lifted by its rope. A dragging bolt may be used if it is firmly tied to the door (not with a reed). For a bolt pressed into the ground, the ברייתא records an argument: the תנא קמא permits and רבי יהודה forbids.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume רבי יהודה is always the lenient one. He is lenient about the dragging bolt but strict about the pressed-in bolt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is his question?
Has he not heard that which was taught:
If it slipped off its rope, it is forbidden; if it was pressed into the ground, it is permitted.
And Rabbi Yehuda says: If it was pressed into the ground,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִשְׁמָט — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: even though it did not slip off its rope, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ? לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא already addresses the case. A bolt that slipped off its rope is forbidden. A pressed-in bolt is permitted according to the תנא קמא and forbidden according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה on a pressed-in bolt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who forbids locking with a bolt pressed into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding a bolt that is pressed into the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the argument from the ברייתא in the last step. The ruling follows the stricter opinion, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 left a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא, who permits, and רבי יהודה, who forbids. שמואל decides it: we are strict, and a pressed-in bolt may not be used to lock the door on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of ...
Pressed or sunk into the ground (said of the bolt)
A bolt or bar used to lock a door

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a תנאים argument into practical הלכה, and it sets up the next question about the reason.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda regarding a bolt pressed into the ground.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is the one who forbids it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנִקְמַז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת quoted from the ברייתא in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bolt pressed into the ground may not be used to lock the door on שבת, following רבי יהודה.

steps.title: What is the reason for forbidding a pressed-in bolt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה forbids a bolt pressed into the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the explanation that comes next. It wants to know why a pressed-in bolt is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling has been given, but the logic behind it is not yet clear. This question is not an attack. It only asks for the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the reason?

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why using a bolt pressed into the ground is forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: it looks like building
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that a bolt pressed into the ground looks like בונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Because it looks like building.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the reason. When the bolt sinks into the ground, it looks like you are building something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is not that real building happens. The problem is that it looks like בונה, because the bolt goes into the ground the way a building part does. Because of how it looks, חכמים forbade it.

keyTerms.meaning: It looks like ...
Building, one of the forbidden מלאכות of שבת

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say this is real building. It is forbidden only because it looks like building.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Because it looks like building.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּמֶיחְזֵי כְּבוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pressed-in bolt looks like בונה, so חכמים forbade it.

steps.title: What if the bolt has a handle?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחומי בר זכריה asks אביי about a bolt that was given a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי בר זכריה asked אביי: If someone made a handle for the bolt, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. What if the bolt is not tied to the door, but someone made a handle for it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that a bolt is allowed if it is tied to the door, or if it is a כלי, like the מחוזא bolt that could be picked up by its rope. The question here is whether a handle is enough to give the bolt the status of a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him a question
A handle
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Nechumei bar Zecharya asked Abaye:
If he made a handle for it, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case, a bolt with a handle, building on the idea from step 9 that a כלי is permitted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a handle gives an untied bolt the status of a כלי.

steps.title: אביי: Then it is like a pestle
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a bolt with a handle is like a pestle, which is clearly a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You are talking about a pestle! (So of course it is permitted.)
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with surprise. A bolt with a handle is like a pestle, and a pestle is clearly a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handle makes the bolt look and work like a real tool, the same way a pestle has a handle. So it is a כלי and may be used even if it is not tied to the door.

keyTerms.meaning: A pestle, a pounding tool with a handle
You are saying

phrases.english: He said to him: A pestle, you are saying!
phrases.notes: In other words, with a handle it is a proper utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוּכְנָא קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A bolt with a handle is like a pestle, a real כלי, so it is permitted.

steps.title: The same ruling stated directly by רב נחומי בר אדא
steps.stepSummary: A parallel version: רב נחומי בר אדא rules that a bolt with a handle is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב נחומי בר אדא said: If he made a handle for it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same idea again, this time as a plain ruling instead of a question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איתמר shows that this teaching was also passed down in another form. Here it is a direct ruling that a handle makes the bolt permitted, which matches אביי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (a teaching passed down by the אמוראים)
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: A bolt that is not tied to the door is permitted if it is a כלי, for example if it has a handle. A bolt pressed into the ground is forbidden because it looks like בונה.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Nechumei bar Adda said:
If he made a handle for it, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַב נְחוּמִי בַּר אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the conclusion of steps 16 and 17 as a direct ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bolt with a handle may be used to lock the door on שבת.

steps.title: The heavy beam in רבי פדת's house
steps.stepSummary: A beam so heavy that ten people were needed to lift it was placed against the door. רבי פדת allowed it because it has the status of a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain beam in רבי פדת's house that took ten people to lift, and they would put it against the door. He did not say anything to them. He said: It has the status of a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story to show how far the idea of a כלי can go. Even a very heavy beam may be used to block the door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think something so big and heavy is like a building part and not a כלי. רבי פדת says it is still a כלי, so leaning it against the door is not building.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam or crossbar
Against the door
It has the legal status of a כלי
And he said nothing to them (he did not object)

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא שָׁרִיתָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַבִּי פְּדָת
phrases.english: There was a certain beam in the house of Rabbi Pedat
that ten people would lift
and they would place it against the door,
and he did not say anything to them.
He said: It has the status of a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שָׁרִיתָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַבִּי פְּדָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'it is a כלי, so it is permitted' idea to a very heavy object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a very heavy beam counts as a כלי and may be placed against the door on שבת.

steps.title: The huge mortar in מר שמואל's house
steps.stepSummary: מר שמואל allowed a mortar holding an אדריבא to be placed against the door, because it has the status of a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain mortar in מר שמואל's house that held an אדריבא (half a כור). מר שמואל allowed them to put it against the door. He said: It has the status of a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story with the same message. A very large mortar may also be used to block the door.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the beam, the mortar is huge, but it is clearly a tool with a purpose. So it keeps the status of a כלי, and using it to secure the door is not בונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortar, a large bowl for pounding grain
A large measure, half a כּוֹר
He permitted

steps.whatToRemember: An object that is a כלי, even a very large and heavy one, may be used to secure a door on שבת, because this does not look like building.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אֲסִיתָא דַּהֲוָת בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: There was a certain mortar in the house of Mar Shmuel
that held an adriva,
Mar Shmuel permitted placing it against the door.
He said: It has the status of a utensil.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אֲסִיתָא דַּהֲוָת בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that confirms the principle of step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A large mortar keeps the status of a כלי and may be placed against the door on שבת.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל asks for רב אסי's teaching on boat arches
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל writes to רב עמרם and asks him to repeat the special teachings he once quoted from רב אסי about the arches of a boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל sent a message to רב עמרם: 'Please tell us some of those excellent teachings you once told us in the name of רב אסי about the arches of a boat.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רמי בר יחזקאל asks רב עמרם to repeat a ruling of רב אסי about boat arches, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boats had curved arches over them, and mats were draped over those arches for shelter. The question is about covering those arches on שבת. Covering something can look like building a tent, which is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent (a message) to him
The arches (hoops) of a boat
Excellent, choice teachings
In the name of

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרַב עַמְרָם:
phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel sent to Rav Amram:
Let the Master tell us
some of those excellent teachings
that you told us in the name of Rav Asi
about the arches of a boat.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרַב עַמְרָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from objects placed against a door (steps 19-20) to a new case about covering structures on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did רב אסי rule about the arches of a boat?

steps.title: רב אסי's ruling: a mat may be spread over boat arches on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם reports רב אסי's ruling. If the arches are a טפח wide, or are less than three טפחים apart, one may spread a mat over them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: This is what רב אסי said. These boat arches, when they are a טפח wide, or even if they are not a טפח wide but there are less than three טפחים between one arch and the next, then on the next day (שבת) one may bring a mat and spread it over them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם answers with רב אסי's ruling. Under two conditions, a person may spread a mat over the boat's arches on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An arch that is a טפח wide already counts as a roof. If the arches are thinner but less than three טפחים apart, the gaps are treated as closed in (the rule of לבוד). Either way, a tent already exists before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, the minimum width to count as a roof
Or alternatively / or even
Three (טפחים); a gap smaller than this is treated as closed (לבוד)
The next day, meaning on שבת
A mat

steps.confusionAlert: The 'less than three טפחים' condition is only needed when the arches are NOT a טפח wide. Arches a טפח wide are enough by themselves, with no condition on spacing.

phrases.english: He sent back to him:
So said Rav Asi:
These arches of a boat,
when they are a handbreadth wide,
or even if they are not a handbreadth wide
but there are not three handbreadths between one and the next,
phrases.notes: Gaps under three טפחים count as closed (לבוד).

phrases.english: on the next day one may bring a mat
and spread it over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If the arches are a טפח wide, or are less than three טפחים apart, one may spread a mat over them on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spreading a mat over qualifying boat arches on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: The reason: it only adds to an existing temporary tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב אסי's ruling. The arches already form a temporary tent, and spreading the mat only adds to it, which is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because this is adding onto a temporary tent, and that is perfectly fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the mat is allowed and answers right away. Spreading the mat only adds to a tent that already exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a new אהל on שבת is forbidden. The arches already count as a temporary tent, so the mat does not create anything new. It only enlarges what is there, and that is מוסיף על אהל עראי, which is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Adding onto a temporary tent (permitted on שבת)
It is perfectly fine / permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key to both cases here. It is also a basic rule in הלכות שבת: you may not start a tent, but you may extend one that already exists.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is adding onto a temporary tent,
and that is perfectly fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב אסי's ruling in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The arches already form a tent, so the mat only adds to a temporary tent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding to an existing temporary tent on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: רב הונא's rams need shade by day and air by night
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא had rams that needed shade during the day and open air at night. He came to רב to ask how to manage this on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא had certain rams that needed shade during the day and fresh air at night. He came before רב.
steps.whatsHappening: A practical story begins. רב הונא brings his problem to רב, and this sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is that the pen must be covered by day and uncovered at night, even on שבת. Spreading a full new cover on שבת morning would be making a new אהל, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams
During the day
Shade
At night
Air, open sky

phrases.aramaic: הָנְהוּ דִּכְרֵי דַּהֲווֹ לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: There were certain rams that belonged to Rav Huna,
which needed shade during the day
and needed air at night.
He came before Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ דִּכְרֵי דַּהֲווֹ לֵיהּ לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, practical case that uses the same rule of adding to a temporary tent.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the rams' pen be covered by day and uncovered at night on שבת without building a new tent?

steps.title: רב's advice: leave one טפח spread so it can be unrolled on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב tells רב הונא to roll up the mat but leave one טפח spread out. The next day he may unroll the rest, because that only adds to a temporary tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go roll up the mat, but leave one handbreadth of it spread out. The next day, unroll it. That is adding onto a temporary tent, and that is perfectly fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical solution that applies the rule just explained. A small piece of tent is left in place, so unrolling the mat on שבת counts only as adding to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טפח that stays spread out is a tent that already exists. Unrolling the rest of the mat on שבת therefore does not start a new tent. It is the same reasoning as the boat arches.

keyTerms.meaning: Roll up
A mat (used for shade)
Leave over
Spread it out / unroll it

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת you may not start a new tent, but you may add to an existing temporary one. Boat arches that count as a roof, or one טפח of mat left spread out, are enough of an existing tent to make adding permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: Rolling up the mat and leaving one טפח spread happens BEFORE שבת. Only the unrolling happens on שבת itself.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go roll up the mat,
and leave a handbreadth of it spread out;
the next day, unroll it,
and it is adding onto a temporary tent,
and that is perfectly fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל כְּרוֹךְ בּוּדְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question from step 24 using the principle stated in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leave a טפח spread out before שבת, then unroll the rest on שבת as an addition to a temporary tent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unrolling a mat on שבת is permitted when one טפח was left spread out beforehand.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Keeping a minimal tent in place before שבת makes it permitted to extend it on שבת.

steps.title: A curtain may be put up and taken down on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoting רבי חייא, rules that a וילון (privacy curtain) may be spread out and taken down on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said in the name of רבי חייא: a curtain may be spread out, and may also be taken down, on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: a hanging curtain may be put up or taken down on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A וילון hangs down like a wall or a door. It does not form a roof over anything. Since it is not an אהל (tent), spreading or removing it does not involve building a tent on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A curtain hung for privacy that works like a wall, not a roof
To spread it out or set it up
To take it down or dismantle it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the boat arches and the rams' mat from earlier. Those covers act as roofs. A curtain only hangs like a wall, so the question of 'adding to a tent' does not come up here.

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
a curtain — it is permitted to spread it out
and it is permitted to take it down on Shabbat.
phrases.notes: It is like a wall or door, not a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of temporary coverings on שבת and moves from roof-like covers to a wall-like curtain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A וילון may be spread out and taken down on שבת.

steps.title: A bridal canopy may be taken down and spread out on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A כילת חתנים (bridal canopy draped over a bed) may be taken down and spread out on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bridal canopy may be taken down and spread out on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב, still quoting רבי חייא, gives a second ruling: a bridal canopy hung over a bed is also permitted. The next steps add limits to this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bridal canopy hangs from a point above the bed and slopes down on both sides. Because it comes to a point, it has no flat roof, and so it is not treated as an אהל. This is why it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Bridal canopy: a cloth hung over a bed that slopes down on both sides from a peak

phrases.english: A bridal canopy —
it is permitted to take it down and to spread it out on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּילַּת חֲתָנִים מוּתָּר לְפוֹרְקָהּ וְלִנְטוֹתָהּ בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same statement of רב in the name of רבי חייא from step 26, adding a second permitted covering after the curtain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כילת חתנים may be taken down and spread out on שבת.

steps.title: First limit: the canopy's top must be less than a handbreadth wide
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי limits the canopy ruling. It applies only if the top is less than a טפח wide. If the top is a טפח wide, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת the son of רב אידי said: we only said this when the canopy's top is less than a טפח wide. But if its top is a טפח wide, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת בריה דרב אידי narrows the previous ruling so that the canopy is permitted only in one shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat top one טפח wide counts as a roof, which makes the canopy an אהל. Putting up a tent on שבת is forbidden. The canopy is permitted only when it comes to a narrow peak with no real roof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We only said this when...': a formula that narrows an earlier ruling
Its roof or top
A handbreadth, the minimum width that counts as a roof

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet the son of Rav Idi said:
We said this only
where its top is not a handbreadth wide,
but if its top is a handbreadth wide, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: A flat top one טפח wide counts as a tent roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין בְּגַגָּהּ טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the bridal canopy ruling from step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The canopy is permitted only if its top is less than a טפח wide.

steps.title: Second limit: no handbreadth of width within three handbreadths of the top
steps.stepSummary: Even when the top is less than a טפח, the canopy is permitted only if it does not widen to a טפח within three טפחים below the peak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when its top is not a טפח wide, we only said it is permitted if it does not reach a טפח of width within three טפחים of the top. But if it does reach a טפח of width within three טפחים of the top, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The limiting continues and adds a second condition about how quickly the canopy widens below the peak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of לבוד, gaps smaller than three טפחים are treated as closed. So if the sloping sides spread to a טפח apart within three טפחים of the peak, that area counts as a roof one טפח wide. This makes it an אהל and forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Less than three טפחים, the distance treated as closed together (לָבוּד)
Near the top or peak

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 28. Step 28 looks only at the very top. This step adds that the area just below the top is also measured, because anything within three טפחים counts as part of the roof.

phrases.english: And even when its top is not a handbreadth wide,
we said this only
where there is not, within less than three handbreadths
near the top, a handbreadth of width,
but if there is, within less than three handbreadths
near the top, a handbreadth of width, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין בְּגַגָּהּ טֶפַח לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stricter condition on top of step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The canopy is forbidden if it reaches a טפח of width within three טפחים of the peak.

steps.title: A third limit begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a third condition that applies even when the second condition is met. The text continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even when there is not a טפח of width within three טפחים of the top, we only said it is permitted where there is not...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: the גמרא is starting yet another limit on the canopy, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern 'and even when... we only said' shows that each condition stacks on the one before. The canopy has to pass every test to be permitted. The content of this third test comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, or even

phrases.english: And even when there is not, within less than three handbreadths
near the top, a handbreadth of width,
we said this only where there is not...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֵין בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה סָמוּךְ לַגַּג טֶפַח נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third stacked condition after step 29.
